title.narrative: Power to You(th) Ethiopia

description.narrative: The Power to You(th) partnership unites Amref Flying Doctors, Rutgers and Sonke Gender Justice (Sonke), all established organisations with synergetic expertise, geographic footprint and networks. This partnership forms a Consortium that believes change starts in communities. To trigger this change, we will strengthen civil society organisations (CSOs) to empower and increase the voice of adolescent girls and young women (AGYW). The Consortium fosters ownership at the country level, with locally formed coalitions and representation of beneficiaries in our governance. As the lead, Amref Flying Doctors, in collaboration with Amref Health Africa (AHA), has always worked from the premise that priorities are set in Africa and that communities drive change.

In the reporting period, the CMT has been providing technical assitance for the 25 CSOs addressed in previous years. We didn�t target new CSO for 2023; however, efforts were yet made to provide continuous support so that CSOs can institutionalize and advance the application of GTA during all phases of project cycle. The CMT is planning to conduct Organizational Capacity Assessmnet of the existing 25 CSOs during March 2024. The CMT may share comprehensive report later.

Like indicator PW2.A2 many CSOs were in need of capacity building on GTA. As a result the project has trained more underserved local CSOs so that they would be enabled to using a Gender and Social Inclusion lens during all phases of the programming cycle with specific attention to youth. So far the CSOs have started integrating GTA in their planning of activities , However power to youth aspires to see these CSOs to be gender transformative so that they go beyond improving the condition of women and girls. So as the project will keep following up to get there in the coming years.

Description of effective use of accountability mechanisms by citizens or communities and CSOs towards SRHR of all people (SRHR I)

comment.narrative: The baseline study found no evidence of (effective) accountability mechanisms in place or in use on SRHR.

18 social accountability committees (SACs) were established in all districts. In some of the districts SACs were established at kebele level. All the committes have recieved training on concepts of social accountablity and national standards and tools. Among these were 5 SAC members from Kewet & South mecha & Asayta & bahirdar districts are being active and effectively contributing to PTY outcomes: They regularly meet and discuss on SRHR and youths issues. Some are bringing outcomes by canceling child marriages, networking and collaboration on services and PTY issues.
We planned to have 1 SAC in Afar and 1 SAC Amhara
Six Social Accountability Committeess were established and strengthened. Participants were youths, women representatives, religious leaders, CSOs.

In this reporting period (2023), there were 3 targets 1) Family law adaptation in Afar region 2) National youth policy revision 3) Directive on the representing young people at Health Center governning board. The country has achieved the third in 2023. MoH has endorsed a directive that entails every health centers should include 2 young people (1M & 1F) as member of health Center board. The other two policy documents (National Youth policy & Afar rgeion Family law) are not yet finalyzed. However, they have progressed about 75%. Draft documents are prepared. Hopefully, they are going to be approved in 2024
MoH has revised Meaningful Youth Engagement guideline and The Ethiopian Orthodox chrch in Bahirdar has prepared guideline to address HPs and SGBV

title.narrative: Young people demand accountability and responsiveness on key issues

# of young people (disaggregate in age brackets and by gender identity who participate in policy and decision-making bodies (disaggregate type and level) and perceive their participation as meaningful (SRHR A)

description.narrative: disaggregated in age brackets and by gender identity for m or x

comment.narrative: In 2022 different opportunities were created for young people who participated on decision making bodies including representation at district council partipate on Adolescent and Youth Council and forums and meeting and challenging national parliament and regional council members (of them 16 are Female).

In the reporting period, the CMT has over achieved this indicator. We were successful in terms of meaningfully engaging young people at decision making bodies. In Ethiopia context, Health centers are managed by boards. By continuously lobbying the sub national government, we were be able to bring 58 youths (29F) at Health center governing boards. The 58 youths were officially assigned to be member of the health center governing boards. This gives them an opportunity to take decision making role on the health center resources including challenging the health system to improve adolescnet and youth helath services.
There was a delay in starting implementation. The ongoing war also affected the program
